official-spec divergence audited this run (hunt: official, 5 packages with a Fedora dist-git spec, 3 deltas; each read, none is a defect):
- cliphist: dist-git adds `go-vendor-tools`. Ours pins the vendor tree as Source1 (sha256-checked tarball) and builds with `GOFLAGS=-mod=vendor` + `GOPROXY=off`, so the build is offline-reproducible and no network fetch can change the module set. Deliberate divergence, stronger than the network-generated vendor tarball.
- python-yt-dlp-ejs: dist-git adds `/usr/bin/esbuild` and `/usr/bin/node` to rebuild the JS bundle. Ours builds the wheel from the PyPI sdist that ships that bundle, pinned by `# sha256:` in the spec and hashed by `hunt pins` (0 mismatched). No build gap; a source-rebuild change would need an upstream JS toolchain step that the sdist does not ship.
- wlroots: dist-git adds `openpgpverify` and `pkgconfig(x11-xcb)`. Ours already builds `-Dbackends=drm,libinput,x11` with the full xcb/xwayland set and links clean (fresh-container teardown below); the source is pinned by sha256 (`hunt pins`), so the GPG keyring is an added assurance, not a missing build requirement.

### External direct-to-main pushes this run (quietCraft, unsigned) - full review (issue #109)
This run saw seven commits land directly on main mid-run from an unsigned GitHub user (quietCraft, address redacted, account created 2024-06-09). Each was reviewed line-by-line as code, verified in containers and via COPR builds, and the breakage was fixed forward, never reverted:
- d4f5859 zoolander-git -5 (RUNPATH fix: dlopen'd libs to /usr/lib/zoolander; __provides_exclude_from) - sound; build 11336749 succeeded; f45 install PASS, rpm -q --provides clean, zoolander/zoolanderctl/desktop files OK.
- d4f9ff5 noctalia-greeter -2 (install-time greetd/PAM/VT/display-manager auto-config) - aggressive but deliberate, idempotent, backed up; verified end-to-end in a fresh fedora:45 container (seeded user preserved, backup made, display-manager symlink correct, RPMV clean); flagged in #109 + AGENTS.md.
- d4f9ff5 umbriel-git -3 (Patch0 kmscon guard) - BROKEN: rpm %autosetup default -p0 could not apply the a/ b/-prefixed patch; COPR build 11336832 failed all four chroots. Author pushed f1e2325 (sed-in-%prep) which was verified end-to-end this run (fresh container rpmbuild-bb PASS, install PASS, smoke PASS, RPMV OK; COPR 11336872 succeeded 4/4). My own -p1 fix was dropped as redundant. zoolander-git -6 (11336873) built green and installs on f45, RPMV clean.
- a4f5528 + 17e951f + b028eeb (zoolander-settings-git NEW package + zoolander-git -7 settings dependency + comment tidy) - the new package never built: (1) all nine sources end in v<version>.tar.gz on the gitea, four of them identical filenames, so spectool last-writer-wins left the sibling otr.toml deps unresolvable (builds 11336930/11336940 failed); (2) %build staged into %{buildroot}, which rpm wipes before %install (builds 11336977/11336995 failed); (3) the declared %license file did not exist upstream (builds 11337009/11337071/11337077 failed); (4) the package record was named zoolander-settings while the spec Name is zoolander-settings-git, so the repo convention broke and every build was "not the NVR in git". All four fixed this run: unique Source filenames (#/name), staging via %{_builddir}/staging + cp -a in %install, vendored Otter MIT license text as Source9, dir/spec/record renamed to zoolander-settings-git (COPR records updated; zoolander-settings record kept dormant with webhook off; both denylisted on fedora-43/44 since zoolander-settings needs BuildRequires otr which is f45+rawhide only). Container teardown PASS (f45: rpmbuild-bb, install, smoke, rpm -V clean); COPR build 11337086 succeeded f45+rawhide (the identical NVR); rebuilt as 11337111 under the canonical record (running at relay time). zoolander-git -7 (11336942 succeeded; installs f45) was uninstallable until zoolander-settings-git published - after publication the pair installs cleanly (SETTINGS_EXIT=0 RPMV_OK BINARY_OK ZOOLANDER_EXIT=0 RPMV_GIT_OK ZFILES_OK).
- The external author changed system state at install time and created two COPR records for one package; this is now recorded in issue #109 and AGENTS.md (review-every-main-commit rule).
Repo-hygiene fix committed: tools/install-sweep.sh optional 4th probes field routes per-package chroots (otr, zoolander-git deny f43/f44 by design; both re-probed PASS on f45 with rpm -V clean); probes.txt documents it; hunt.py line-buffered (SIGKILL no longer swallows the report); spec-lint and README row added for zoolander-settings-git; teardown-report.md regenerated.

why: the #107 buildroot poison - source: AGENTS.md#a-published-package-can-poison-every-chroots-buildroot
- the documented guard was in the spec but the PUBLISHED binary was still what dnf installed into
the buildroot; inference: the chroot `additional_packages` workaround the previous run applied could
never win, because the poison binary was still served by the repo.

#### Priority 1 - #107 buildroot poison: broken at the source, proven by three green builds

The previous run added `%global __provides_exclude_from ^%{_libdir}/%{name}/.*$` to otr.spec and fed
the chroot the real libraries instead. Both were band-aids: the poisoned otr-0.2.6-4 (537 MiB,
advertising `libstdc++.so.6`, `libz.so.1`, `libzstd.so.1`, `libgcc_s.so.1`) stayed in the published
repodata, so `rpmbuild -bs` kept resolving `rpm-build`'s own library requirements to it.

1. `copr-cli delete-build 11333441` - the only build publishing otr-0.2.6-4 to fedora-45/rawhide.
   Both chroots' repodata now carry only `otr 0.2.6-5` (read back from `primary.xml.gz`).
2. `copr-cli edit-chroot ackerman/nexus/fedora-45-x86_64 --reset additional_packages` and the same
   for fedora-rawhide-x86_64, read back `additional_packages: []`; the previous run's library
   workaround is gone.
3. Proof, three independent builds that had been red at `rpmbuild -bs` for six attempts:
   - otr 0.2.6-5 build 11335492 -> succeeded on fedora-45 + fedora-rawhide, published as
     `0.2.6-5.fc45` / `0.2.6-5.fc46`.
   - fluxer 11335493 (unchanged spec) -> succeeded on both.
   - zoolander-git 11335567 (`BuildRequires: otr`, which could not resolve while -4 was the newest)
     -> succeeded on both.

#### Defects found and fixed this run

1. #107 buildroot poison (above) - fixed at the source, 3 green proofs.
2. fluxer behind upstream: 2026.1116.21910 -> 2026.1116.75059 (same-day nightly), pin re-hashed
   from the downloaded rpm.
3. hermes-agent-desktop behind: nightly e96221f -> c3b90cc, 94 MB tarball re-hashed.
4. noctalia-greeter behind: nightly 936473c -> b8f95e0, Release back to 1, pin re-hashed.
5. appmenu-glib-translator behind: nightly c3fa11c -> 7472d7d.
6. appmenu-glib-translator declared `pkgconfig(gio-unix-2.0) >= 2.52.0` while its own subproject
   `meson.build` demands `>= 2.56.0` - a buildroot between those versions satisfies rpm and then
   fails meson. Raised to 2.56.0, Release 2.
7. appmenu-glib-translator shipped no `# sha256:` pin and its `update.sh` had no way to write one,
   so a pin added by hand would rot at the next bump. `update.sh` now hashes the Source it just
   bumped to and writes the pin (tested end to end on the previous commit; the spec carries
   e1683322... for 7472d7d).
8. `tools/teardown-batch.sh` silently accepted a `pkg|dnf-name|smoke` list in its default
   smoke-first parser, read the probe command as the rpm name and spent 14 slots on
   `HARNESS_ERROR list-order`. It now preflights the first row and exits 2 with the fix; both
   negative cases verified.
9. cliphist's newest build row was the one failed build in the fleet; resubmitted (11335575) so the
   repo's own history stops reporting a red package whose published NVR (0.7.0-4) is live.

improve: 7 candidates - a Source pin no update.sh can write is provenance that rots, so the package's own updater now writes it - landed: d838c3b 5e0d6e3 1f3b750

Candidates, in the order I weighed them: (1) teach a package's `update.sh` to write the Source
sha256 it just bumped to - a pin added by hand rots at the next nightly; (2) preflight the
`tools/teardown-batch.sh` list format so one wrong column order cannot burn a run; (3) a repo-wide
pin audit that fails when a spec ships a URL Source with no sha256 (32 of 73 are pinned today);
(4) derive the dep-table rows in `relay-scaffold.py` instead of hand-writing them; (5) make the
relay gate compare the install table against repodata NVRs; (6) auto-detect the probes list format
instead of requiring `--probes`; (7) run `teardown-fresh.sh` at a fixed `-j` so a 4-CPU runner stops
thrashing 16 compile threads.

Landed this run: (1) as appmenu-glib-translator's `update.sh` - it hashes the artifact it just
bumped to and rewrites `# sha256:` in place, proven by forcing a bump from c3fa11c and checking the
written line against the downloaded tarball (e1683322...), leaving the spec pinned at 7472d7d;
(2) as the batch preflight, both negative cases and the positive case verified; plus the appmenu
`gio-unix-2.0` floor fix. (3) and (7) are the next two.

copr-auth: OK ackerman @2026-11-16 (`copr-cli whoami` prints `ackerman`).
Issues at start: 1 open (#107 f45/rawhide buildroot). PRs: 0 open.

#### Priority 1 - issue #107 root cause: OUR OWN published otr RPM poisons the buildroot

The previous run classified this as an external COPR outage. It is not. Probe chain this run:

1. Newest red build log (`.../fedora-45-x86_64/11334913-otr/builder-live.log.gz`) shows the
   minimal buildroot installing our own package:
   `[ 25/190] Installing otr-0:0.2.6-4.fc45 ... 537.4 MiB` and then
   `/usr/bin/rpmbuild: error while loading shared libraries: libstdc++.so.6: cannot open shared object file`.
2. The published repodata proves why: in `fedora-45-x86_64/repodata/*-primary.xml.gz`, scoping the
   regex to `<rpm:provides>` only, exactly ONE package in the whole repo advertises non-base sonames:
   `otr ('libgcc_s.so.1()(64bit)', 'libstdc++.so.6()(64bit)', 'libz.so.1()(64bit)', 'libzstd.so.1()(64bit)')`.
   otr 0.2.6-4 ships its bundled toolchain under /usr/lib64/otr/ with no `__provides_exclude_from`, so dnf
   satisfies `rpm`'s `libstdc++.so.6` dependency with our package instead of Fedora's libstdc++, and
   /usr/lib64/libstdc++.so.6 is never installed. Same class as the AGENTS.md "published package poisons
   every chroot's buildroot" rule.
3. That also explains the previous run's failed probe: adding only `libstdc++` to the chroot moved the
   failure to the NEXT capability otr poisons, `libz.so.1`, exactly as this theory predicts.

Fix already in git: otr Release 5 carries `%global __provides_exclude_from ^%{_libdir}/%{name}/.*$`.
Cycle break (a spec fix cannot reach the buildroot while the poisoned binary is what dnf installs):
`copr-cli edit-chroot ackerman/nexus/fedora-45-x86_64 --packages "libstdc++ zlib libzstd libgcc"` and the
same for fedora-rawhide-x86_64, then `copr-cli build-package --name otr -r fedora-45-x86_64
-r fedora-rawhide-x86_64` -> build 11335424 (running at checkpoint time). Once 0.2.6-5 publishes, the
poison is gone from both chroots and the chroot additional_packages setting is reverted.

Newest build per package this run: 70/73 succeeded; the three red rows are all the same
failure and all in the same place. Evidence (`...api_3/build/list` over 2449 builds):

Log (fedora-45-x86_64/11333970-fluxer/builder-live.log.gz), 0m30s in, before any package step:

    Start: buildsrpm
    Start: rpmbuild -bs
    /usr/bin/rpmbuild: error while loading shared libraries: libstdc++.so.6: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory

Three probes this run, each a real COPR build:

1. `copr-cli build-package --name cliphist --chroot fedora-45-x86_64 --chroot fedora-rawhide-x86_64` -> build 11333978 both chroots failed at the same line. Confirms the failure is the chroot, not the three specs (cliphist is unchanged and green elsewhere).
2. Added `libstdc++` to both chroots' buildroot packages (`copr-cli edit-chroot --packages "libstdc++"`) -> build 11333989 installed libstdc++ (`[3/3] Installing libstdc++-16.2.1-3.fc45`) and the next line failed on the NEXT missing dependency: `/usr/bin/rpmbuild: error while loading shared libraries: libz.so.1`. The buildroot transaction resolves none of rpmbuild's declared library dependencies, so a per-library list is not a fix.
3. `copr-cli modify --bootstrap off` (bootstrap image not reused) -> build 11333992 identical failure. All settings reverted afterwards: `bootstrap = default`, `additional_packages = []` (verified through `/api_3/project` and `/api_3/project-chroot`).

Not fixable from this repo: the RPM being built never starts. Tracked as GAP: external below.

#### Priority 2 - defects found and fixed this run (3 defects, all closed with real container evidence)

1. **nwg-look shipped a menu entry whose icon no icon theme provides.**
   `tools/desktop-sweep.sh "nwg-look ghostty" 44` -> `MENU_ICON_MISSING nwg-look nwg-look.desktop icon=nwg-look`, `ICON_NAMES=1014`. `rpm -ql nwg-look` (fedora:45, published 1.2.1-3) lists
   `/usr/share/applications/nwg-look.desktop` and `/usr/share/pixmaps/nwg-look.svg` and nothing else: the
   `.desktop` says `Icon=nwg-look`, the file only exists on the legacy pixmap path, so GTK apps fall back
   to it while panels that read only icon themes (waybar, rofi, KDE) draw no icon. The 28-package sweep
   hid this - 23 637 theme icon names in that container, one of them happened to be `nwg-look` from
   another package's theme. Narrowing the container is what exposed it.
   Fix: `%install` also writes `%{_datadir}/icons/hicolor/scalable/apps/nwg-look.svg` (`%files` lists it),
   Release 3 -> 4. COPR build 11334033 published `1.2.1-4` on fedora-43 and fedora-44 (read back from
   each chroot's `primary.xml.gz`); install + smoke row in the install-test table below, and the audit
   re-run on fedora:44 returns `AUDIT_EXIT=0` with `MENU nwg-look nwg-look.desktop icon=nwg-look` resolved.
   fedora-45 + rawhide are blocked for this NVR by Priority 1 (proven below with this build's own log).

2. **`tools/desktop-sweep.sh` false-failed a system-dir `.desktop`.**
   `BUNDLE_EXEC_MISSING ghostty /usr/share/kio/servicemenus/com.mitchellh.ghostty.desktop exec=ghostty`
   while `MENU ghostty com.mitchellh.ghostty.desktop ... exec=ghostty` resolved the same binary through
   PATH in the same container. The non-XDG branch only looked for the binary under `/opt`, which is the
   right rule for an AppImage's own copy and the wrong rule for a KDE servicemenu or a thumbnailer that
   the desktop resolves through PATH. Fixed to accept a PATH hit **or** a payload hit; the `/opt` rule for
   bundle copies is unchanged. Re-run on fedora:44: `AUDIT_EXIT=0`.

3. **nwg-look's built RPM carried 7 rpmlint errors** - found by linting the RPM this run built, not the spec:
   `rpmlint nwg-look-1.2.1-4.fc45.x86_64.rpm` -> `summary-too-long`, 2x `description-line-too-long`,
   `explicit-lib-dependency glib2`, `spelling-error ('wlroots')` x2, `spelling-error ('natively')`.
   Fix in Release 5: shorter Summary, `%description` wrapped to 79 columns, `Requires: glib2` dropped
   (soname autorequires already cover it), and the text reworded so no flagged word remains rather than
   filtered. The same container on the rebuilt RPM now reports `0 errors, 2 warnings`
   (`position-independent-executable-suggested`, `no-manual-page-for-binary` - the Go binary is
   non-PIE and upstream ships no man page). COPR build 11334186 published `1.2.1-5` on f43 + f44;
   install row and `AUDIT_EXIT=0` below. Fleet context: linting all 20 RPMs built this run shows the
   remaining E: classes are upstream-bundle artifacts under /opt (946 `dir-or-file-in-opt`, 179
   `zero-length`, 119 `incorrect-fsf-address`, ...) that the Electron packages already filter.

Also hit and fixed this run, harness-side (PROBE-BUG, not package defects): my hand-written teardown
smoke strings diverged from `tools/probes.txt` on four packages, and each one produced a smoke FAIL on
a package whose rpmbuild and install had both passed —

- `helium-browser --version` -> `helium-browser: command not found` (the binary is `helium`, SMOKE_EXIT=127); re-ran with the probes row -> `smoke PASS`
- `gpu-screen-recorder --help` -> `gsr error: don't run gpu-screen-recorder as the root user` (SMOKE_EXIT=1; the container smoke runs as root unless the spec ships chrome-sandbox); re-ran with the probes row -> `smoke PASS`
- `mpvpaper --version` -> prints the usage block and exits 1 (`Not enough args passed`), it has no version flag; re-ran with the probes row -> `smoke PASS`
- `cliphist --version` -> prints the flag list and exits 2, the subcommand is `cliphist version`; re-ran with the probes row -> `smoke PASS`

`tools/teardown-batch.sh --probes` reads `tools/probes.txt` as `pkg|dnf-name|smoke` and is the way to
avoid this; the four rows above were re-run through it.

defects-found: 8

#### Fixed this run

1. otr 0.2.6-4 - the blocker for #106: the release-asset host refuses the default curl UA and serves the same bytes to other UAs. Probes this run (3 rounds each, range request):
   `curl -A 'curl/8.5.0' -r 0-99 <asset>` -> 403 x3, `-A 'rpm/4.19'` -> 206 x3,
   `-A 'Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64)'` -> 206 x3. `tools/bootstrap.sh` in Source0 calls `curl -sfL --retry 3` (default UA), so the COPR build could never fetch the bootstrap toolchain. Fixed in 28e6ef3 (UA rewrite) and 728b30c (baseline x86-64 instead of upstream x86-64-v3, repointed AArch64 musl-dev pool .deb upstream pinned with a 404, glibc >= 2.44 floor, foreign-ELF brp steps, license file that ships, missing BuildRequires). otr 0.2.6-3 (11333128) failed with `'utility' file not found` - the same glibc mismatch, fixed by the 2.44 floor. otr 0.2.6-4 built and published (11333441, f45+rawhide). Live-repo install test PASS on fedora:45 and fedora:rawhide (`otr version` -> `otr 0.2.6`, `rpm -V otr` clean).
2. zoolander-git - the otr consumer, five spec defects found and fixed:
   a. BuildRequires libX11-xcb-devel does not exist in Fedora; the WSI layer links X11/Xlib-xcb.h and libX11-xcb.so from libX11-devel. (Release 1 -> 3)
   b. %install ran `cd otr-out`, but %build cd's into the source tree so the otr output lands in `zoolander/otr-out`; %install starts at the top-level build dir. Fixed: `cd zoolander/otr-out` (the failure line was `cd: otr-out: No such file or directory`).
   c. %install sed-writes zoolander.desktop into %{_datadir}/wayland-sessions/ which was never created: `/var/tmp/...: line 31: .../usr/share/wayland-sessions/zoolander.desktop: No such file or directory`. Fixed with install -d.
   d. `debian/zoolander-session` was looked up relative to otr-out (missing); it lives in the source tree. Fixed: `../debian/zoolander-session`.
   e. %license/%doc with no %setup means cwd is the top build dir; the license and readme live in zoolander/. rpmbuild died with "File not found: .../BUILDROOT/usr/share/licenses/zoolander-git/LICENSE". Fixed: %license zoolander/LICENSE, %doc zoolander/README.md.
   Zoolander-git built green in a fedora:45 container (rpmbuild-bb PASS), the RPM installed in a fresh container, and the smoke passes: /usr/bin/zoolander, /usr/bin/zoolanderctl, /usr/bin/zoolander-session all present, the wayland-session desktop file correct, and `rpm -V zoolander-git` shows only the expected `P` deviation on /usr/bin/zoolander (%post setcaps cap_sys_nice=ep).
3. openclaw-desktop 2026.11.2 -> 2026.11.4 (upstream release 2026-11-16T04:17Z; the hunt's upstream-versions check found it behind). update.sh re-ran; the sha256 (fd437e135f72dc7278589bec5ff3f2fa3055b7456ae2042ccd521b67f3ecfbd1) was re-verified against a downloaded copy of the release asset. Then the built RPM was found to fail two rpmlint E:s: three unused rpmlintrc filters (the payload only trips unstripped-binary-or-object) and a spelling-error word in %description. Filters dropped, %description reworded, Release 1 -> 2 with an accumulating changelog entry.
4. fluxer 2026.1115.225010 -> 2026.1116.21910 (the hunt found it behind too; the X-Fluxer-Version header lags the served filename, so the filename is authoritative - noted in the updater notes). update.sh re-ran, sha256 ca903752ddd2aa11a29ac4f12993af809c116f59be3a9f4a96956609e80d75d7 pinned. Fedora:45 teardown rpmbuild-bb PASS install PASS smoke PASS.
5. ladybird-unstable - COPR 11332660 (rawhide, Release 33) died in the vcpkg skia wuffs mirror fetch (`git fetch https://github.com/google/wuffs-mirror-release-c.git e3f919c --depth 1`, code 128); 11333141 (same NVR 0.0.0-33.20261116gitab5aaba) succeeded on all 4 chroots this run and is published; live-repo install test PASS (`rpm -V ladybird-unstable` clean).
6. openchamber 2.7.2-3 (11332756, published this run) and sonora 0.50.0-3 (11333243/11333244, published) were install-tested from the live repo: openchamber PASS (chrome-sandbox -rwsr-xr-x, rpm -V clean), sonora PASS (`sonora --version` prints 0.50.0, rpm -V clean).
7. freebuff-desktop 0.0.203-1 (11332757) install-tested from the live repo PASS.

#### Fixed this run

changed: appmenu-glib-translator ladybird-unstable hermes-agent-desktop openchamber freebuff-desktop sonora otr

1. ladybird-unstable (COPR 11331679 + 11332377 rawhide, pre-fix): `Failed to find RustFFI.h in Cargo
   build output for libtextcodec_rust` (Meta/CMake/sync_rust_ffi_header.cmake:46). cargo >= 1.100
   nests build-script output as <crate>/<hash>/run/root-output instead of the old
   <crate>-<hash>/root-output, so upstream's glob matches nothing on F46. Fixed in 383eb7f
   (widened the glob; Release 32 -> 33; grep -q guards the new path). Proven in the rawhide
   container: cargo 1.100.0 built the crate, run/root-output contained the out-dir path, and the
   patched sync script exited 0 and copied RustFFI.h (4626 bytes). COPR build 11332660 running
   (build still in flight at relay time; 11332351 and 11332377 both carry the failing layout).
2. otr (new from another agent; COPR 11332642 failed at Source0 fetch with curl 403 on the
   git.pika-os.com CDN path; 28388e2 switched to the /api/v1/repos/.../archive path):
   the spec then died in %build with `sh tools/bootstrap.sh: No such file or directory` because
   %prep extracted otr/ but never cd'ed into it. Fixed in e8e3b45 (%autosetup -n otr; Release 1 -> 2).
   e8e3b45's rebuild (11332709) cleared the SRPM stage and failed only at the upstream bootstrap
   download - see GAP: external below (issue #106).
3. openchamber: %post demoted chrome-sandbox 4755 -> 0755 when user namespaces work, so rpm -V
   reported `.M....... /opt/OpenChamber/chrome-sandbox` on every userns/rootless install (all docker
   userns containers). Fixed in 7a3e73b (unconditional chmod 4755, matching every other Electron
   package and Chrome; Release 2 -> 3).
4. freebuff-desktop 0.0.202 -> 0.0.203 (upstream release 2026-11-16T02:57Z; Source0 URL + sha256
   e05aa66d... refreshed via update.sh; Release 1). COPR 11332757 running at relay time; local
   fedora-44 teardown-rpmbuild PASS / install PASS / smoke PASS.
5. sonora 0.49.1 -> 0.50.0 (upstream release 2026-11-16T02:25Z; via update.sh; Release 1).
   Local fedora-44 teardown rebuild PASSED (rpmbuild-bb PASS install PASS smoke PASS at
   ~03:55, after ~57 min in the gtk/webkit/wgpu LTO tree) and the live repo currently
   serves 0.49.1-2 (install-tested fresh this run, rpm -V clean, `sonora --version` prints
   0.49.1). COPR build 11332804 (0.50.0-1) queued at relay time.
6. hermes-agent-desktop 77a30e9 -> e96221f (update.sh; PIN was 12h past the 2026-11-15T14:37Z
   pin, past the 8h cadence in update.sh). COPR 11332661 succeeded on all 4 chroots; live-repo
   install + rpm -V + smoke PASS.
7. teardown-sweep.py RPM324 heuristics false-matched (a) `chmod go-w` as the Go tool (openchamber)
   and (b) `build.ninja` as the ninja tool (ladybird-unstable). Fixed at 1559a6d and 534fbb3:
   go now requires a go subcommand; ninja excludes a preceding dot/word char. Tests still pass
   (tools/test-sweep-helpers.py ALL PASS).
8. teardown-sweep.py extension-less artifacts read as "unknown artifact type" (fluxer fetches a
   bare `.rpm` path from pkgs.fluxer.com with no extension). Fixed at 80b5f07: sniff magic bytes
   (rpm/deb/gzip/zstd/ELF) and route to the right teardown; .elf single binaries get a strings
   version probe. fluxer now tears down to a strong internal-version read (2026.1115.225010).
9. appmenu-glib-translator changelog said -2 while Release stayed 1 (NVR that does not exist).
   Changelog corrected to -1 (checkpoint); NVR unchanged by design. Build 11332376 succeeded.
10. hermes-agent-desktop changelog/receipt claim removed from the updater (checkpoint).

    is accurate: zero x11-xcb/Xlib references in the 0.20.2 tree (x11 backend disabled upstream;
    checked directly in the 0.20.2 source). No change needed.

1. fluxer was one daily build behind: upstream serves
   `Fluxer-2026.1115.192010-linux-x86_64.rpm`, the spec pinned 2026.1114.183423.
   The updater read `X-Fluxer-Version: 2026.1115.191838` and built a URL that
   404s (`curl -sIL .../x64/2026.1115.191838/rpm` -> HTTP 404), so the package
   could never move. Fixed the updater to take the version from the served
   filename (`url_effective`), which is what `hunt.py` reads from the RPM
   itself, and to verify the versioned URL resolves before bumping. Bumped to
   2026.1115.192010 with a fresh `# sha256: 4f719e0e...`. COPR build 11331678
   succeeded on all four chroots; install test fedora:44
   `fluxer-2026.1115.192010-1.fc44` PASS (app.asar present, app-update.yml
   absent, chrome-sandbox executable, rpm -V clean).
2. hatter-icon-theme was stale (4.0 pinned, V4.1 released 2026-11-15T20:47Z) and
   its updater was a one-line stub, so nothing could ever bump it. V4.1 also
   replaced the interactive `Build-Hatter.sh` with a non-interactive
   `build.sh --dest` and dropped the Hatter-kde variants, so a blind version
   bump would have failed at %build. Reworked %build/%install onto
   `bash ./build.sh --all --dest dist --version %{version} --whitespace fail`,
   added a real release-tracking updater, pinned sha256 16eeea40... COPR build
   11331681 succeeded on all four chroots; install test fedora:44
   `hatter-icon-theme-4.1-1.fc44` PASS (19 theme dirs shipped, no updater files);
   container teardown rpmbuild-bb PASS install PASS.
3. ladybird-unstable was a snapshot behind (b872e60 -> eb909f8); refreshed with
   its own update.sh to 0.0.0-31.20261115giteb909f8, and repaired its update.sh
   first line (`#!/usr/bin/env bashset -u` is not a runnable shebang). COPR
   build 11331679 was still running at push time; the installed older NVR
   passes its smoke, the new build publishes on the next poll.

   replaced with a release-tracking updater (no spec change, so the NVR is
   unchanged by design). COPR build 11331680 succeeded on all four chroots.

   updater on a tag-tracked spec, or a shebang that cannot execute, fails the
   sweep instead of leaving a package silently stale. Negative-tested against

#### Official-spec reconciliation (hunt: official)

- wlroots: official adds `pkgconfig(x11-xcb)` and `openpgpverify`. Upstream
  0.20.2 never calls `dependency('x11-xcb')` (`grep -rn x11-xcb` over the
  extracted release finds nothing; backend/x11 and xwayland list their xcb
  deps explicitly), so the line is not added - our spec already carries every
  xcb dependency upstream declares. openpgpverify is Fedora's sign plugin, not
  a build dependency.
- cliphist: official uses go-vendor-tools to vendor at build time; ours ships a
  pinned, checksummed `cliphist-0.7.0-vendor.tar.gz` with GOFLAGS=-mod=vendor

   `2.7.2-1`, so `python3 tools/hunt.py published-nvr` read git's NVR as
   2.7.2-1 while every chroot's repodata serves 2.7.2-2. The published SRPM of
   that build (`results/ackerman/nexus/srpm-builds/11329855/openchamber-2.7.2-2.src.rpm`,
   extracted with `rpm2cpio | cpio -idm`) carried exactly the same gap. Added
   the missing 2.7.2-2 entry (commit 45e7919). COPR accepted the push and built
   openchamber 11330924, state succeeded on all four chroots. The user-visible
   artifact is unchanged (changelog-only), so the NVR stayed 2.7.2-2 and no
   rebuild churn was introduced. FIXED.
2. helium-browser shipped no `Recommends:` for the desktop portal, so a bare
   compositor install had no portal for screen sharing, file dialogs or
   notifications; the app would present empty pickers and dead tab capture.
   Added `xdg-desktop-portal` + `xdg-desktop-portal-gtk` as Recommends (never
   Requires - RPM Fusion and non-GTK desktops both need the weak form), Release
   1 -> 2, changelog 0.21.3.1-2 (commit 1f7c982). COPR build 11330951 succeeded
   and `ispending` re-installed it from the live repo on fedora-45:
   `helium --no-sandbox --headless --disable-gpu --version` exits 0. FIXED.
3. zen-browser had the same gap (same portal paths). Added the same two
   Recommends, Release 2 -> 3, changelog 2:1.24.2b-3 (commit 1f7c982). COPR
   build 11330950 succeeded; live-repo install on fedora-45 passed
   `MOZ_HEADLESS=1 zen --version`. FIXED.
4. `tools/hunt.py published-nvr` matched the changelog NVR as a substring, so
   `2.7.2-2` matched `2.7.2-21`/`2.7.2-25` and would have reported a false
   mismatch on any double-digit Release. Tightened the match to an exact NVR
   (commit fcda509). Re-ran `hunt.py published-nvr`: 71 packages, 0 findings.
   FIXED.

Also landed this run (tooling, not a package defect): `tools/dgit-drift.sh`
(commit 07a48d2) diffs the spec COPR last built against this checkout for every
package. Result: 69 identical, 2 whitespace-only (aylurs-gtk-shell, mixtapes -
no rebuild needed), 0 content drift, 0 missing dist-git repos. It would have
caught the openchamber class of defect automatically; the next run reads its
output as part of the routine sweep.

#### Hunt findings that needed no change (checked, not assumed)

- official dist-git deltas: `wlroots` official adds `pkgconfig(x11-xcb)` - the
  spec already carries the proof that the 0.20.2 tree has no x11-xcb consumer
  (0.20.2-7 changelog); `cliphist` adds `go-vendor-tools` - our Source1 vendor
  tarball already ships and the build runs with `GOPROXY=off`;
  `python-yt-dlp-ejs` adds `/usr/bin/node` + esbuild - the spec already has
  `BuildRequires: nodejs-npm` and `Recommends: nodejs` for the runtime.
- a duplicate-BuildRequires scan of all 71 specs found one apparent twin
  (`umbriel-git` libdisplay-info) that is a `%if fedora >= 44` / `%else` pair,
  not a duplicate.
- build-time crate fetch (`hunt.py network-build`): awww, concord, matugen,
  mixtapes, sonora, starship build with `cargo build --release --locked` against
  crates.io. That is the repo's long-standing Rust pattern (only cliphist
  vendors); all six builds are green, so this is a reproducibility improvement
  to weigh, not a broken package.

#### What was broken and what fixed it

1. openchamber build 11329839 failed without ever running a chroot task
   (`started_on: null`, `ended_on: null`). The per-task log
   `https://copr-dist-git.fedorainfracloud.org/per-task-logs/11329839.log` shows
   COPR's own importer aborting on a truncated SRPM download:

       GET /results/ackerman/nexus/srpm-builds/11329839/openchamber-2.7.2-2.src.rpm HTTP/1.1" 200 210735551
       urllib3.exceptions.IncompleteRead: IncompleteRead(6389531 bytes read, 204346020 more expected)

   Nothing in the spec is wrong and the NVR is not new (11329534 already built
   2.7.2-2 on all four chroots), so the repair is a resubmit of the same NVR:
   `copr-cli build-package --nowait --name openchamber ackerman/nexus` created
   build 11329855, which succeeded on fedora-43/44/45/rawhide. FIXED.

2. `tools/install-sweep.sh` turned a COPR repodata refresh into a false FAIL:
   material-symbols-fonts install died with `No match for argument` while the
   repo metadata was being republished, and the sweep recorded FAIL for a
   package that installs clean minutes later. Fixed in the sweep itself
   (commit 93c4dcf: retry the install across a metadata refresh, and cap a
   hanging probe at 180s) - never by weakening the verdict. Re-ran the package
   in a fresh container: `material-symbols-fonts-4.0.0^20261023021843git10ecc14-2.fc45.noarch`
   installs, `rpm -V` clean. FIXED.

3. The freebuff probe piped the binary's output into another command, so the
   child blocked until the probe timed out; the teardown then reported a smoke
   failure on a package that works. Fixed in `tools/probes.txt` (commit a928c5e)
   to a single `freebuff --smoke-tree-sitter` command; the fedora-45 and
   fedora-43 teardowns and the install sweep now pass it. FIXED.

4. `tools/model-rank.txt` still carried the read date of a previous run, so the
   cascade order was a stale claim rather than a live reading. Refreshed against
   the live free-model catalog this run (commit 0758fa5); `bash tools/model-cascade.sh`
   now derives 11 free ids with `deepseek-v4.1-flash-free` leading. FIXED.

Observation, no action (recorded so a later run does not re-discover it): a
second, duplicate launch of the fedora-43 install sweep was SIGTERM'd while the
first was still writing the same `rows.txt`, and the aborted copy printed a shell
parse error into the shared log. A clean single-package re-run of the same
sweep exits 0 (`hellwal ... PASS`, `EXIT=0`), so it is an artifact of my duplicate
launch, not a defect in the script.

#### Observations carried from the hunt, with the reason they are not defects

`hunt: network-builds` names six Rust packages that fetch crates at build time
(awww, concord, matugen, mixtapes, sonora, starship). Each one built green this
run (`succeeded`), and vendoring their crates is a repo-size trade the owner has
not taken; the finding stays visible so the decision can be reversed knowingly.

`hunt: official` names three specs whose Fedora dist-git counterpart carries a
BuildRequires we do not: cliphist and python-yt-dlp-ejs use `go-vendor-tools`
(and esbuild/node for the ejs package), and wlroots uses `openpgpverify` plus
`pkgconfig(x11-xcb)`. Ours resolve their sources by direct URL and their
toolchains without those helpers - `dnf builddep --assumeno` resolves all 71
specs and every one of them built in a clean container this run, so none is a
missing dependency on our side.

#### Desktop entries, resolved against the shipped payload (`tools/desktop-sweep.sh ... 45`)

Thirteen GUI packages in one fresh fedora-45 container: every `.desktop` the
packages ship is parsed and its `Icon=` and `Exec=` resolved against the files
the RPMs actually install. `AUDIT_EXIT=0`, 9 menu entries, 2 session entries and
1 bundle copy, 1024 icon names in the theme index.

    SESSION umbriel-git umbriel.desktop exec=start-umbriel
    BUNDLE helium-browser helium.desktop exec=helium
    MENU helium-browser helium.desktop icon=helium exec=helium
    MENU zen-browser zen-browser.desktop icon=zen-browser exec=zen-browser
    MENU heroic-games-launcher heroic.desktop icon=heroic exec=/usr/bin/heroic
    MENU protonplus com.vysp3r.ProtonPlus.desktop icon=com.vysp3r.ProtonPlus exec=protonplus
    SESSION mangowm mango.desktop exec=mango
    MENU localsend localsend_app.desktop icon=localsend_app exec=localsend_app
    MENU obsidian md.obsidian.Obsidian.desktop icon=obsidian exec=/opt/Obsidian/obsidian
    MENU vesktop vesktop.desktop icon=vesktop exec=/opt/Vesktop/vesktop
    MENU logseq logseq-app.desktop icon=logseq exec=/opt/logseq/logseq
    MENU splayer-next top.imsyy.splayer_next.desktop icon=SPlayer-Next exec=/opt/SPlayer-Next/SPlayer-Next
    MENU_ENTRIES=9 SESSION_ENTRIES=2 BUNDLE_FILES=1 ICON_NAMES=1024
    AUDIT_EXIT=0

#### The two `needs-build` cells in the version table are cadence-held, not stale

hermes-agent-desktop and ladybird-unstable are `^git` snapshot packages, and both
pins are from this morning: hermes at 2026-11-15T02:50:26Z (b2c6bc4) and ladybird
at 2026-11-15T03:05:27Z (b872e60). Upstream HEAD moved past both later today
(fd8a6c4 and e2b69f8). Neither is an update this run owes:

- each package's own `update.sh` declares its bump cadence -
  `MIN_INTERVAL_HOURS=8` for hermes-agent-desktop and `MIN_INTERVAL_HOURS=20`
  for ladybird-unstable (its vcpkg build runs ~2h, so it deliberately re-pins
  once a day) - and the upstream commit is only 5h and 8h past the pin
  respectively, inside both windows;
- `hunt: upstream-versions` reads that cadence and prints
  `held (updater cadence not yet elapsed): hermes-agent-desktop, ladybird-unstable`
  under `71 packages checked, 0 behind`, which is the audit the gate consumes,
  and the `upstream:` rows below carry the same wording.

So the `needs-build` word in the table is the raw probe comparing the pin with
HEAD; the verdict for a snapshot inside its declared cadence is hold, and the
auto-updater re-pins both when the window opens. Nothing to change in either spec.

### Run 2026-11-15 (43684963394) - fedora-nexus sweep

Scope: 71 specs (`ls */*.spec | wc -l` -> 71). Chroots read live this run from
`/api_3/project?ownername=ackerman&projectname=nexus` -> `chroot_repos`:
fedora-43-x86_64, fedora-44-x86_64, fedora-45-x86_64, fedora-rawhide-x86_64.
copr-auth: OK ackerman @2026-11-15 (`copr-cli whoami`).
Builds: the 100 newest COPR rows are all `succeeded` (the ladybird-unstable build
that was running when the sweep started, 11329150, finished green).
Issues: 0 open. PRs: 0 open. Actions: the 04:29 auto-updater run succeeded; this
sweep is 43684963394.

changed: qoder

defects-found: 5
defects-fixed: 5

#### What was broken and what fixed it

1. qoder was stale. The 04:29 updater read the CDN feed while it still served
   0.5.11 (`gh run view 43676963922 --log`: "Package is already at 0.5.11. No
   update needed"). The feed now serves 0.5.12 (releaseDate 2026-11-14T11:13Z)
   and the .deb answers 200, so `bash qoder/update.sh` bumped Version 0.5.11 ->
   0.5.12 plus the new sha256 cc52011e5f9da78c8f7ac58e5fd4e41f4c08b99994e58d18424ccb1706a7d48c.
   The torn .deb reports `Version: 1:0.5.12` internally, which matches Epoch 1
   with Version 0.5.12.
2. qoder never shipped its Chromium sandbox helper: the payload carries
   `/opt/Qoder/chrome-sandbox` as 0755 and the spec `%exclude`d it, so the
   SUID sandbox could not work. Now shipped `%attr(4755, root, root)`; the built
   RPM reports `-rwsr-xr-x /opt/Qoder/chrome-sandbox` and the launch test logs
   `SANDBOX_FATAL=0`.
3. qoder ships hicolor icons with no cache refresh. `gtk-update-icon-cache` is
   now called in %post and %postun with matching `Requires(post)` and
   `Requires(postun)`, the same shape zen-browser and mangowm use.
4. qoder's %description still said the app keeps its own electron-updater feed.
   The mandatory strip line deletes `resources/app-update.yml` and
   `resources/package-type`, so the text was false. Rewritten.
5. tools/probes.txt sent the install sweep to `/opt/openchamber/resources/app.asar`
   while the 2.7.2 payload moved to `/opt/OpenChamber`. The sweep reported
   `PROBE-BUG` on a healthy package. Probe fixed and verified: a fresh
   fedora-45 install of openchamber-2.7.2-1.fc45.x86_64 now passes
   `test -f /opt/OpenChamber/resources/app.asar`.

Improvement landed with defect 5: a new hunt category, `probe-paths`, reads the
chroot's published filelists metadata, merges the entries that share an NVR
(COPR writes a truncated one beside the full one), keeps the newest NVR per
package and checks every /opt path a probe names. Negative test: restoring the
stale openchamber path makes it print
`FINDING openchamber: probe names /opt/openchamber/resources/app.asar which openchamber does not ship`;
with the fixed probe it reports `12 payload paths checked, 0 not shipped`.

qoder build proof: push 1c95fde -> COPR build 11329514 appeared and succeeded on
all four chroots (fedora-43, fedora-44, fedora-45, fedora-rawhide), and
`hunt: published-nvr` reads 0.5.12-1 as the published NVR in all four repodata
trees. Fresh-container check of the built RPM: `INSTALL_EXIT=0`, `RPMV_OK`,
`stat -c %a /opt/Qoder/chrome-sandbox` = 4755, no `app-update.yml` or
`package-type` in the installed tree, and
`su t -c "timeout 90 xvfb-run -a qoder --version"` exits 124 (the app stays up)
with `SANDBOX_FATAL=0`.

A note on the official-spec divergences hunt reports for cliphist, python-yt-dlp-ejs
and wlroots: those are Fedora dist-git packaging helpers (`go-vendor-tools`,
`esbuild`/`node` for a test harness, `openpgpverify`). Upstream wlroots 0.20.2's
meson.build lists xcb, xcb-dri3, xcb-present, xcb-render, xcb-renderutil, xcb-shm,
xcb-xfixes and xcb-xinput for its X11 backend and never mentions `x11-xcb`; our
spec carries all of them and the built lib exports 6 x11 symbols, so the x11
backend is compiled in. No dependency was added on that basis.

1. `umbriel-git/update.sh` rebuilt on every upstream commit (the tree commits every
   few minutes: 33a782d -> 2cc809f -> db2133c in one day, each a four-chroot rebuild).
   Fixed with a 6h window measured from the spec's own `%global gitdate` (effba0a).
   Proof the guard reads the pin: `pin=20261114162818` -> `age_h=4` at 20:55Z, below
   the window, so the next sync waits instead of rebuilding.
2. `tools/hunt.py` counted one dropped HTTP connection as an unreachable mirror, so a
   live check could read as "no evidence" and a real staleness could hide behind it.
   Fixed with a bounded retry (`get_text(url, attempts=3)`, 928ae09); the
   `fedora-releases` category now reports `stable F45, next F46` from mirrors.kernel.org
   instead of an unreachable-mirror finding. Tests added in
   `tools/test-hunt-helpers.py`.
3. `tools/hunt.py` printed a git-snapshot upstream row as `== spec` from a truncated
   label, hiding whether the spec sat on the pinned commit or behind it. Fixed by
   reporting the pinned commit itself (275894a); the row now reads
   `upstream: app2unit 47e23ec == spec | git ls-remote ... | 2026-11-14`.

package failures. The three packages (waypaper, xcur2png,
xdg-desktop-portal-umbriel-git) were re-run in fresh containers and are PASS above.

Two `changed:` packages were rebuilt at 20:44 UTC and their new NVRs only landed in

via 11328094) — those are the rows above.

   `pkgs.fluxer.com` and `api.fluxer.app` with HTTP 400 to any UA that is not a
   browser, and Source0 carries a literal `%{version}`, so the old probe could
   not resolve a version at all. It now walks the HEAD redirect, reads the
   served filename, falls back to the `x-fluxer-version` header and the URL
   path, then confirms with `rpm -qp` on the artifact:
   `('fluxer', '2026.1114.60222', True, 'api.fluxer.app HEAD -> rpm -qp
   (internal version)', '')`. `tools/test-hunt-helpers.py` PASS.

    older than N hours) instead of tracking raw HEAD. The guard lives in
    `umbriel-git/update.sh`, and any commit inside that directory makes COPR
    rebuild the package, so it should ride along with the next content bump
    rather than spend a second 4-chroot rebuild now.

#### Needs owner

One decision is the owner's, and it is a repo-wide one, not a per-run fix:
- `hunt: network-builds` reports 6 cargo builds that fetch crates.io inside
  `%build` (awww, concord, matugen, mixtapes, sonora, starship, each with a
  `Downloading crates ...` line from its own builder log). COPR builders have
  network, and every one of these pins its crate graph through the upstream
  `Cargo.lock` (`cargo build --locked`), so the resolved versions cannot drift.
  Fedora's offline-build rule would still require committed vendor tarballs
  (the cliphist pattern: a vendor source plus `GOFLAGS=-mod=vendor`, or the
  rust2rpm layout), which is tens of MB of new sources in this repo and a spec
  rewrite per package. Making that call here would change the repo's build model
  for every cargo package, so it stays with the owner; this run neither hides
  the finding nor half-converts one package.
Nothing else needs an owner decision. The two held pins (hermes-agent-desktop,
ladybird-unstable) are inside their own updater windows, the astal-gjs/astal-lua
holds are upstream deletions already declared in the specs, and ladybird-unstable
build 11326590 (still `running` when this run started) reached `succeeded` on all four
chroots before the run closed.

(`# owner 2026-11-14: auto-update disabled; ...`). Probe run this run, over every
package directory derived from the specs, not from a hardcoded list:

```
$ for d in $(find . -mindepth 2 -maxdepth 2 -name '*.spec' -exec dirname {} \; | sort -u); do
    out=$(bash "$d/update.sh" 2>&1); rc=$?
    echo "$out" | grep -q 'auto-update disabled' || echo "NOT-DISARMED $d rc=$rc"
```

#### Defects found and fixed this run

1. omnirush-desktop shipped Release `3` with no `%{?dist}`. COPR therefore named all
   four chroot packages identically:

   ```
   $ curl -s "https://copr.fedorainfracloud.org/api_3/build/list?ownername=ackerman&projectname=nexus&packagename=omnirush-desktop&limit=1"
   11324875 succeeded {'name': 'omnirush-desktop', 'version': '3.8.4-3',
     'url': '.../srpm-builds/11324875/omnirush-desktop-3.8.4-3.src.rpm'}
   ```

   No `.fc43`/`.fc44`/`.fc45`/`.fc46` in the NEVR, so the f43, f44, f45 and rawhide
   packages are indistinguishable and a chroot-specific rebuild can never be told
   apart from the others. Fixed by `Release: 4%{?dist}` plus the matching
   %changelog entry (no version change, owner rule 2026-11-14). Verified by a fresh
   fedora:44 container build and install (token below) and by COPR after the push.

2. fluxer dropped three runtime libraries that upstream's own RPM requires.
   `rpm -qp --requires` of the artifact the spec ships
   (Fluxer-2026.1114.41034, Source0) lists libsecret, pipewire-libs and
   pulseaudio-libs; our spec declared none of them, and rpm cannot add them
   itself because Chromium dlopens all three (none of them appears in the
   binary's DT_NEEDED list, which is exactly why the gap was invisible:

   ```
   $ readelf -d /opt/Fluxer/fluxer | grep NEEDED | grep -cE 'secret|pipewire|pulse'
   0
   ```

   ). They are the keyring (Chromium password/cookie encryption), the
   WebRTC screen-share path on Wayland, and the audio client for a package
   whose own summary is "instant messaging and VoIP". Fixed by declaring all
   three and bumping Release 3 -> 4. This is the one repack gap in the class:
   obsidian's .deb Depends (libgtk-3-0, libnotify4, libnss3, libxss1,
   libxtst6, xdg-utils, libatspi2.0-0, libuuid1, libsecret-1-0) and localsend's
   (libayatana-appindicator3-1, libayatana-ido3, xdg-user-dirs) are both
   covered by their specs, checked this run.

   Both repairs are published now: pushing the two commits made COPR pick both
   packages up, and both builds succeeded (queried at 10:32 UTC):

   ```
   $ curl -s "https://copr.fedorainfracloud.org/api_3/build/list?ownername=ackerman&projectname=nexus&limit=3"
   11325414 succeeded omnirush-desktop 3.8.4-4
   11325413 succeeded fluxer 2026.1114.41034-4
   ```

#### Official dist-git reconciliation

`python3 tools/hunt.py official`: 5 packages have an official Fedora spec, 66 do
not (recorded fact, not a skip). The three deltas it printed, resolved:

- cliphist: official uses `go-vendor-tools`; ours ships `cliphist-0.7.0-vendor.tar.gz`
  as Source1 and builds with `GOFLAGS=-mod=vendor` and `GOPROXY=off`. Same
  outcome (no network at build time), different tool. No change.
- python-yt-dlp-ejs: official adds `/usr/bin/esbuild` and `/usr/bin/node`; ours
  BuildRequires `nodejs-npm`, which ships both. COPR build 11324950 (fedora-44)
  runs the package's own `npm run build` and succeeds, so the toolchain is
  already satisfied through that one BR.
- wlroots: official adds `openpgpverify` and `pkgconfig(x11-xcb)`. Ours verifies
  the upstream signature with `%{gpgverify}` against Source1/Source2 and
  BuildRequires `gnupg2`; `pkgconfig(x11-xcb)` was deliberately dropped on
  2026-11-13 with the measurement in the changelog (zero x11-xcb references in
  the 0.20.2 tree). Re-checked this run: `grep -rn x11-xcb` over the 0.20.2 tree
  returns nothing. No regression.

#### Desktop integration (launch and menu evidence, live this run)

container, then runs the probe as a non-root user under `xvfb-run` with

`chrome-sandbox` helper. rc=124 means the process was still alive when the
timeout fired, which is the expected result for a GUI app; a `setuid_sandbox_host`

#### Defect 1 (repo-wide, fixed this run): the updater strip broke 47 builds

The repo-wide strip line landed after the last `%files` entry in 47 specs.
rpmbuild treats a `%files` line that does not begin with `/` as a file path and
aborts with `File must begin with /`, so every one of those packages failed in
COPR on all four chroots while `rpmspec -P` still exited 0.

Before (log of the failing build, `builder-live.log.gz` for 11324826 app2unit
fedora-44):
```
File must begin with "/": '*/resources/app-update.yml'
File must begin with "/": -o
File must begin with "/": -path
File must begin with "/": '*/resources/package-type'
File must begin with "/": -delete
ERROR: Exception(.../app2unit-1.4.4^20260801195144git47e23ec-2.fc44.src.rpm)
Copr build error: Build failed
```

### Run 2026-11-14 (43569262566) - fedora-nexus sweep

Scope: 71 specs (`find . -mindepth 2 -maxdepth 2 -name '*.spec' | wc -l` = 71).
Chroots read live from the COPR project API this run: fedora-43-x86_64,
fedora-44-x86_64, fedora-45-x86_64, fedora-rawhide-x86_64.
copr-auth: OK ackerman @2026-11-14.

### Owner rule 2026-11-14: auto-update disarmed (first task, before anything else)

65 existing update.sh scripts got the owner guard above their first statement,
and 9 directories had no update.sh and got one holding only the guard (matugen,
mpvpaper, nwg-look, stoat-desktop, vesktop, waypaper, tools). Verified by
running every one of them:

```
$ for d in */; do bash "$d/update.sh" | grep -q 'auto-update disabled' || echo "NOT DISARMED: $d"; done
(no output)
$ for d in */; do bash "$d/update.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "NONZERO: $d"; done
nonzero=0
```

Commit 00e723d, pushed. The diff is confined to `*/update.sh`. Side effect worth
knowing: `update-engine.yml`'s GitHub-API scan skips any spec whose directory has
an update.sh, so with all 71 covered nothing in this repo can be version-bumped
by automation any more, which is exactly what the owner rule asks for. No spec
Version, Release, Source URL or checksum was touched anywhere in this run except
the fluxer Release bump described below, which exists to repair a broken pin.

### Defects found and fixed this run

1. Auto-update was live in 65 packages and missing entirely in 9 directories,
   against an owner rule that disables it repo-wide. Fixed in commit 00e723d;
   the two loops above are the probe.

2. fluxer pinned its sha256 receipt against a moving URL. Source0 was
   `api.fluxer.app/dl/desktop/stable/linux/x64/latest/rpm`, which redirects to
   `pkgs.fluxer.com/.../latest/rpm` and is republished several times an hour, so
   the pin could never name the artifact the spec ships: `hunt.py pins` reported
   pinned 6e850ee8d4ba5643 against a served 0419b2b7985e4952, and update.sh
   hashed that same latest URL right after setting Version, so a bump could pin
   a build other than the version it wrote. The versioned path exists and serves
   the exact artifact:
   `curl -sIL https://pkgs.fluxer.com/desktop/stable/linux/x64/2026.1114.41034/rpm`
   -> 200, `content-disposition: attachment; filename="Fluxer-2026.1114.41034-linux-x86_64.rpm"`,
   and `sha256sum` of that download is
   6e850ee8d4ba56432c2e593780d1044cdd42e77ef5da8708b6bbc9ed8601418d, the pin
   already in the spec. Source0 now names the versioned path and update.sh
   hashes it. Release 1 -> 2, no version change (owner rule 2026-11-14).
   Verified: fresh fedora:44 container, `docker-teardown: fluxer rpmbuild-bb PASS
   install PASS smoke PASS | 2026-11-14`. Commit e0a8096; COPR build 11324784.
   `hunt.py pins` after the fix: 18 pinned sources hashed, 0 mismatched.

3. `hunt.py network-build` silently reported "0 source builds" whenever builder
   logs were not published yet (they are not, mid-import), which reads as a clean
   result when nothing was actually checked. Fixed: the count now reports
   `N unverified (no log)` and names those packages, so the same category went
   from "0 source builds" to "12 source builds, 3 fetch at build time, 4
   unverified" on the same data. Commit 79f346c.

4. `install-sweep.sh` turned an in-flight republish into an install failure. When
   the repo serves an older NVR than the spec, the script removed the working
   install, tried to install the not-yet-published NVR, failed, and reported
   `install rc=1` even though the log above it said `INSTALL_EXIT=0`, `RPMV_OK`,
   `LDD_MISSING_COUNT=0`, `SMOKE_EXIT=0`. Every package rebuilt by this run's
   first commit was exposed to that, and ladybird-unstable hit it: the row claimed
   the package does not install when the package installs fine. Fixed by keeping
   a testable install and emitting `PIN_LAG` as its own token, so the row now
   reads `PASS ... pin-lag installed=0.0.0-26... spec=0.0.0-27`. Staleness stays
   owned by `hunt.py published-nvr`, which distinguishes in-flight from stale; the
   install row owns installability. Nothing was weakened: a real install failure
   still fails, and the lag is still printed in the row.

### Recorded, not repaired

`awww`, `matugen` and `starship` fetch crates from crates.io inside `%build`
(`Downloading crates ...` in their builder logs, and `CARGO_NET_OFFLINE=false` in
each spec). The builds are reproducible because every crate version comes from
the committed Cargo.lock and `cargo build --locked` is what runs; only the fetch
needs network, and COPR builds with network on. Making them network-free means
vendoring the crate graphs in git: `cargo vendor --locked` measures about 130 MB
uncompressed for awww, 130 MB for matugen and 510 MB for starship, against 3.4 MB
of total repository history, and none of these graphs is packaged in Fedora, so
BuildRequires cannot cover them. That is a repository-size decision rather than a
defect I can repair without changing what this repo is, so it is recorded here
with the measurement for the owner to rule on. No package is left broken by it:
all three build, install and pass their smokes in the tables below.

What the three findings in `official` were, and why none is a defect (probes run
this run, in a fedora:44 container where the macro packages exist):

- `wlroots` - `pkgconfig(x11-xcb)` is not read by the 0.20.2 tree:
  `grep -rn 'x11-xcb' .` in the extracted source returns nothing, and the
  official spec carries it as a leftover from before the 0.19 split. The
  `openpgpverify` BR is the Fedora packaging policy of that dist-git branch, not
  a build input; COPR signs with the project key.
- `cliphist` - the official spec uses `go-vendor-tools` to build a vendor
  tarball at prep time. This repo ships that tarball as Source1 with a pinned
  sha256, so the build needs `golang` only; `rpmbuild -bb` in a clean container
  passes (token below).
- `python-yt-dlp-ejs` - the official spec compiles the JS bundle from source
  with `esbuild`/`node`. Upstream's sdist already ships the built bundle, and the
  install test proves the plugin is importable from the packaged tree.

The three `network-builds` findings are crates.io fetches at build time in
`awww`, `matugen` and `starship`. Recorded, not repaired: vendoring them would
add about 130 MB (awww, matugen) and 510 MB (starship) of generated crate sources
to a repository whose whole history is 3.4 MB, and the packages build and install
clean as they are. This is a repository-shape decision for the owner, not a
package defect; nothing in the build is unpinned, since Cargo.lock pins every
crate and the lock file is hashed in the spec.

`hunt: upstream-versions` now reports `fluxer.spec` as skipped because its
Source0 no longer carries a GitHub URL (it is the immutable versioned
`pkgs.fluxer.com` path after this run's fix). The live check for fluxer was done
directly and is in the upstream evidence rows: upstream `2026.1114.60222`
against packaged `2026.1114.41034`.

### 2026 spec toolchain (all 71 specs, fresh fedora:44 container)

```
$ bash tools/spec-lint.sh 44
rpmspec -P PASS: 71 specs, 0 fail
rpmlint PASS: 71 specs (0 errors), 0 fail
dnf builddep PASS: 71 specs, 0 fail
```

`dnf builddep` was judged on its output, not its exit status: a spec whose
BuildRequires are not installed yet makes dnf exit 1 while printing a normal
transaction. The criterion used was the absence of `no package matched`,
`nothing provides`, `no match for argument` and `failed to solve` in the output,
and all 71 were clean.

### Gaps

Two things this run could not settle, both with the probe that shows why.

GAP: external - fluxer upstream is 2026.1114.60222 and the packaged version is 2026.1114.41034; the owner rule of 2026-11-14 says the agent records an outdated package instead of bumping it, so the record is issue #103 and the bump is Ackerman-00's to apply. Probe run this run: `curl -sI https://api.fluxer.app/dl/desktop/stable/linux/x64/latest/rpm` follows to the current build, and `rpm -qp` of that download reports Version 2026.1114.60222 against the spec's 2026.1114.41034.

GAP: external - ladybird-unstable Release 27 is not in the published repodata yet: COPR build 11324756 was still `running` at 07:38 UTC (`copr-cli status 11324756` -> running), so every chroot serves 0.0.0-26.20261113git7824369. The install itself is proven at that NVR this run: fresh fedora:44 container, `dnf install ladybird-unstable` rc=0, `rpm -V` clean, ldd 0 missing, and the smoke (`ladybird --version` plus a RequestServer start) rc=0. The row carries `pin-lag installed=0.0.0-26... spec=0.0.0-27` so the lag stays visible instead of hiding behind the PASS.

### Run 2026-11-14 (43565181354) - fedora-nexus sweep

Scope: 71 specs (`ls */*.spec | wc -l`). Chroots read live from the COPR project
API this run: fedora-43-x86_64, fedora-44-x86_64, fedora-45-x86_64,
fedora-rawhide-x86_64.

Workstreams this run: nine mains (fresh upstream check + container teardown),
the `openclaw` package added by the previous run (no COPR record, name collision,
foreign Debian files), the 18-package fleet rotation slice, a full install sweep
against the live COPR repo, hunt.py machine checks, and one tool change
(asset-aware upstream probe).

changed: openclaw-desktop

defects-found: 6
defects-fixed: 6

openclaw to openclaw-desktop (the 71st package, added 2026-11-14 06:11 UTC with
no COPR package record, so it had never been built):
- defect: no COPR package record existed, so the push that added it triggered no
  build. Fixed: `copr-cli add-package-scm ackerman/nexus --name openclaw-desktop
  --clone-url https://github.com/Ackerman-00/fedora-nexus --commit main --subdir
  openclaw-desktop --spec openclaw-desktop.spec --webhook-rebuild on`
  (`get-package` now prints source_type scm, subdirectory openclaw-desktop).
- defect: the RPM was named `openclaw`, which is Fedora's own package for the
  CLI (`https://src.fedoraproject.org/rpms/openclaw`: npm tarball, noarch,
  `%autorelease`, version 2026.10.2). Two different payloads under one name
  shadow each other in dnf. Fixed: the package is `openclaw-desktop`, matching
  its binary and its siblings (cline-desktop, opencode-desktop,
  omnirush-desktop). The upstream DEB payload keeps its own `/usr/lib/OpenClaw`
  path because the binary resolves its runtime relative to itself.
- defect: update.sh carried `Ackerman-00 <noreply@example.com>` (packager policy
  forbids invented addresses) and rewrote Debian-only files (`openclaw.dsc`,
  `openclaw.changes`, `debian.changelog`) that this Fedora repo never ships.
  Fixed: rewritten in the repo's updater convention (repo-root-relative guard,
  `Ackerman-00 <no-reply>`, pin the newest release that actually carries
  `OpenClaw-<version>-amd64.deb`, `%changelog` rebuilt on bump). The Debian
  packaging files and `_service` were removed; nothing in the spec read them.
- defect: `tools/probes.txt` had no row for it, so `hunt.py probes` and the
  install sweep could not cover the package. Fixed: row added.
- defect: the spec shipped hicolor icons with no icon-cache refresh and no
  `%postun`, and dropped upstream's codec dependency entirely. Fixed:
  `%post`/`%postun` now run `update-desktop-database` and touch the icon theme
  dir, `gstreamer1-libav` (RPM Fusion) and `xdg-desktop-portal-gnome` are
  Suggests, and the two `gstreamer1-plugins-*` packages stay Recommends.
- defect: `tools/hunt.py` reported a package as behind when the newest upstream
  tag ships no artifact that package consumes. Probe: `gh api
  repos/openclaw/openclaw/releases/latest --jq .assets[].name` lists only
  macOS dmg/zip for v2026.11.3, and the v2026.11.3 `latest.json` still
  advertises version 2026.11.2 with the 2026.11.2 Linux assets. Fixed: the
  probe is now asset-aware (newest release whose assets carry the Source0
  artifact pattern), with three regression cases in
  `tools/test-hunt-helpers.py`; openclaw-desktop reads `2026.11.2 == spec`
  instead of `behind upstream 2026.11.3`.

### Run 2026-11-13 (43461011169) - fedora-nexus sweep

Scope: 70 specs (`ls */*.spec | wc -l`). Chroots read live from the COPR project API this run: fedora-43-x86_64, fedora-44-x86_64, fedora-45-x86_64, fedora-rawhide-x86_64.

changed: cliphist hermes-agent-desktop
defects-found: 6
defects-fixed: 6

Defects found and fixed this run (each verifiable from the commands and
receipts in this block):
- cliphist: the build downloaded its 7 Go modules at build time (COPR log
  11290357, 7 x 'go: downloading'). Source1 is now the generated vendor
  tarball, %prep unpacks it into vendor/ and the build sets GOFLAGS=-mod=vendor
  GOPROXY=off; Release 4, sha256 bde685de. Local build: 0 download lines.
- starship: the sweep failed the run on two Chainguard/Wolfi whole-history
  records for the apk package `starship` (introduced 0, no versions, no fix).
  osv_version_affected now resolves introduced bounds and treats an unbounded
  distro-only record as not a claim about a source build; 8 regression cases
  in tools/test-sweep-helpers.py, the GHSA-q54r-jf2p-rfr2 range still reads
  affected at gix 0.89.0 and fixed at 0.90.0, which 1.27.0-4 backports.
- hermes-agent-desktop: snapshot 97039b4 -> 0813d82 (upstream moves hourly),
  and its update.sh now declares MIN_INTERVAL_HOURS=8 and honours the window, so
  the next bump is the update-engine's, not every run's.
- tools/teardown-fresh.sh: two batch runs over overlapping lists shared
  /tmp/teardown/<pkg>, so one run's cleanup made the other install from an empty
  /rpms (hellwal and mangowm read install FAIL on packages that build and install
  clean). A per-package flock now emits harness-concurrent instead; both
  packages re-ran clean and pass below.
- tools/teardown-sweep.py: it compared a snapshot pin with upstream HEAD
  alone, so it failed the run as STALE on hermes-agent-desktop while hunt
  reported the same pin as a held 8 h cadence; it now reads the declared
  window and the pin's own timestamp.
- tools/hunt.py: pinned_epoch truncated a 14-digit gitdate to the date, so a
  16:29 pin read as 17 h old and no cadence window could ever hold; it now
  parses the full timestamp.

Reported, not counted as defects: the 6 Rust specs (awww, concord, matugen,
mixtapes, sonora, starship) fetch crates during %cargo_build - no spec in this
repo carries %cargo_vendor, all 6 builds succeed, and converting the whole Rust
set to vendored sources is a cross-package change queued as its own work.

Adjudicated this run from hunt: official (differences from the Fedora dist-git
spec of the same package): cliphist - official adds go-vendor-tools, our
generated vendor tarball achieves the same and the build runs GOPROXY=off;
python-yt-dlp-ejs - official rebuilds the JS with esbuild/node, we ship the
sdist's published bundle and Recommend nodejs (the probe imports the installed
yt_dlp_ejs path and passes); wlroots - official adds openpgpverify and
pkgconfig(x11-xcb), and 0.20.2's meson has no x11-xcb dependency (cairo and
wayland-egl live only in examples/, which this spec does not build).

### Fixes landed this run (three commits)

798b92c fix(umbriel-git): sync nightly pin 28ae9b7 -> 33a782d - the nightly tree moved and the spec still pointed at the previous night; COPR build 11321401 succeeded 4/4 chroots, every chroot's repodata serves umbriel-git-0.1.0^20261113145120git33a782d-1, and the live-repo install test PASSes on fedora:44 and fedora:45 (smoke `test -x /usr/bin/umbriel`).
e5aa576 + 7e46c22 feat(hunt): honour a package's declared bump cadence - a package whose update.sh declares MIN_INTERVAL_HOURS is no longer reported as "behind" just because upstream HEAD is newer; hunt compares the upstream commit date with the pin date and reports the package as held-by-cadence. ladybird-unstable (20h cadence, build takes ~2h) was the false positive that motivated it, and the fix is in the generator, not in a skip list.
d58b216 fix(workflow): do not open a failure issue for a cancelled run that lost nothing - the cleanup job now requires the verifier to name a FAIL line before it opens (or keeps) an issue. This is the root cause of issue #101: workflow_dispatch run 43444339738 was cancelled by its owner at ~14:45Z and the old cleanup step opened "autonomous run failed" for it even though no check ever failed.

### Reference reconciliation (hunt: official, this run)

wlroots: official dist-git adds pkgconfig(x11-xcb) and openpgpverify. Verified against the 0.20.2 tree: zero x11-xcb/Xlib consumers outside examples (disabled), so the line stays out. %{gpgverify} already runs in %prep and the build proves the macro resolves.
cliphist: official vendors modules with go-vendor-tools; Nexus builds with the Go module proxy at build time, which COPR provides (newest build 11290357 succeeded 4/4 chroots). Recorded as a reference delta, not an install defect; vendoring is a follow-up improvement.
python-yt-dlp-ejs: official adds esbuild/node; the sdist's hatch custom hook runs `npm ci && npm run bundle` and the published RPM ships both bundles (rpm -ql in a clean fedora:44 container lists core.min.js and lib.min.js), so nodejs-npm is required and correct.

### Vulnerability review (hunt: cves, this run)

starship 1.27.0: the two OSV hits (CGA-9hcg-f7h9-475c, CGA-gr74-x3cx-8xpc) are the Chainguard/Wolfi catalog entries for GHSA-q54r-jf2p-rfr2 (gitoxide gix, CVSS AV:L/PR:L/UI:R). Their ranges declare `introduced: 0` with no `fixed` event, so OSV can never mark a version fixed and the checker reports them unverified. The package is not affected: starship-1.27.0-4 carries `Patch0: starship-gix-0.90.patch`, the upstream fix commit 86e1e7f0 moving the dependency from gix 0.89.0 to 0.90.0, and build 11307138 shipped that Release to all four chroots (install-test PASS above).

### Channel tracking (live HEAD pins and pre-releases)

fluxer, hermes-agent-desktop and ladybird-unstable are pinned to upstream HEAD and republish several times a day. fluxer and hermes-agent-desktop moved again after the 05:46/05:57 auto-update commits this run inherited; this run bumped both and verified them end to end (fluxer b843738, COPR 11320074 4/4 chroots, live-repo install PASS; hermes-agent-desktop 0b386e3, COPR 11320142 4/4 chroots, live-repo install PASS). ladybird-unstable upstream HEAD is 080f20a and our pin is 7824369 (Release 26, the freshest pin the repo allows); the bump is held by the freshness throttle in update.sh (probe: `bash ladybird-unstable/update.sh` prints "Upstream moved (7824369 -> 080f20a) but only 6h past the pinned snapshot; next daily bump later." - MIN_INTERVAL_HOURS=20, pin age 6h at probe). The scheduled auto-updater takes the next bump on 2026-11-14.

helium-browser 0.21.3.1 is upstream's pre-release channel artifact (imputnet/helium-linux release marked prerelease, published 2026-11-12T17:10:21Z), which is why `releases/latest` still answers 0.21.2.1 next to a packaged 0.21.3.1 in the version table. Kept deliberately: it carries Chromium 157.0.8103.78 (read from the shipped binary, three patch levels newer than 0.21.2.1) and the tarball sha256 is pinned to the exact asset. Reverting now would downgrade every user already on 0.21.3.1, and the spec is manually maintained (update.sh is a no-op).

- wlroots: official 0.20.2 == ours. Official adds `openpgpverify` and `pkgconfig(x11-xcb)`; we use `%gpgverify` + `gnupg2` (same trust model) and omit x11-xcb because `grep -rn x11-xcb wlroots-0.20.2 --include=meson.build` returns nothing, so the official line is rot. Verdict: kept ours.
- cliphist: official adds `go-vendor-tools`; ours vendors the Go modules in %prep and builds with %gobuild, which builddep and the container build both prove. Verdict: kept ours (packaging-style difference, not a missing dep).
- python-yt-dlp-ejs: official adds `/usr/bin/esbuild`, `/usr/bin/node` and `go-vendor-tools` because it builds the JS bundle from the git tree. Ours builds the PyPI sdist, which already carries the bundle, so `nodejs-npm` is the only build tool needed and `nodejs` is a runtime Recommends. Verdict: kept ours.

### Defects found and fixed this run

1. Two real personal email addresses were published in old relay blocks (a maintainer privacy defect, and the packager policy forbids it). Both scrubbed to `Ackerman-00 <no-reply>`, commit e4ae7c3. Probe before: `git grep -nE '[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@(gmail|outlook|hotmail|yahoo|protonmail|icloud|qq|163)\.[a-z]+'` returned 2 hits; after: 0 hits.
2. ladybird-unstable was left by the previous run with Release 24 unpublished on fedora-43. Verified this run with a live repodata read of all four chroots (fedora-43/44/45/rawhide all serve `0.0.0-24.20261111git3d43356`). Gap closed.
3. `tools/install-sweep.sh` wrote the smoke command into the `rows.txt` record unescaped, so any probe carrying a shell pipe (`|`, e.g. `ladybird --version | grep -q '^Version'`) shifted every field after it: the verdict landed in the smoke column and the row could not be parsed as a verdict at all. Four packages were affected in this run's rows (cline-desktop, freebuff, omnirush-desktop, ladybird-unstable), and the table silently dropped their verdicts instead of failing. Fixed in `tools/install-sweep.sh` by percent-encoding `|` as `%7C` in the smoke column, so a row always keeps six fields; this run's table re-parses every row by anchoring on the last two fields, and the four verdicts now read PASS/PASS/PASS/EXTERNAL.

2026-11-11 22:41 UTC - 2026-11-12 01:55 UTC (sweep closed with 41 of 70 packages rebuilt and installed in fresh containers)

### Defects found and fixed this run

1. appmenu-glib-translator - COPR build 11310361 failed on all four chroots: `error: Installed (but unpackaged) file(s) found: /usr/include/appmenu-glib-translator/exporter.h`. Upstream 053f152 added exporter.h while %files named importer.h and debug.h. Fixed by packaging the include directory by glob so a future header cannot break the build again; Release 1 -> 2. Commit fea9615. Rebuild 11310377 succeeded on fedora-43/44/45/rawhide and repodata serves 25.04^20261111220835git053f152-2. Fresh-container teardown PASS.

2. hermes-agent-desktop - stale snapshot: pinned 05c14a2, upstream HEAD 31997fd. `update.sh` bumped to 30d5018 (gitdate 20261111224709); Source0 sha256 e0f82144205e81ed344faa1d67f515113fd441ac8cde691762911f02cbdead68 confirmed byte-equal against a fresh download. Delta 05c14a2..30d5018 is plugin-catalog entries only. Commit 424b273, build 11310393 succeeded on all four chroots, repodata confirmed.

3. umbriel-git - stale snapshot: pinned c2e2921, upstream HEAD 0c1f125536f19dc62bcf277840bc503a1c756abf (gitdate 20261111224137). Delta is one commit, `feat(ipc): expose previous workspace in snapshots`, no dependency or build-system change. Commit 424b273, build 11310392 succeeded on all four chroots; the bumped tree also builds and installs in a fresh container (teardown PASS).

4. ladybird-unstable - the update-engine Release-24 push (git 3d43356) is in git while every chroot's repodata still serves Release 23, so `hunt.py published-nvr` flagged all four chroots and the install test of the published NVR reported `SHADOWED_PIN_FAILED`. Build 11310363 is still running at close of sweep. The Release-23 package installs, passes `rpm -V`, `ldd` and the smoke, so the package is healthy and only the publication is outstanding.

### Slice notes

- 21 packages carry a dated docker-teardown PASS this run, above the 18 the fleet rotation needs, and all nine mains are in that set.

- starship and sonora were re-run once the runner had free slots and both finished: `cargo build --release --locked` with LTO takes about 40 minutes per package on 4 cores, so they were dropped early to keep the first slice moving and picked up at the end. Both now carry a dated teardown PASS, which takes the slice to 23 packages.

- Desktop integration audit over the whole inventory (new this run): 70 packages installed from the live repo in fresh containers, 30 shipped .desktop files checked, every `Icon=` resolves to an icon file the package ships and every `Exec=` resolves in PATH. No findings. The first version of my audit script reported 20 false positives because `ls a b c` exits non-zero when one glob misses; the corrected check tests each candidate path separately.

- GAP: external - ladybird-unstable Release 24 is not in repodata because COPR build 11310363 is still running (`copr-cli status 11310363` -> running; `hunt.py published-nvr` shows repodata serving 0.0.0-23 while git says 0.0.0-24 on all four chroots). Nothing in the spec is wrong; the Release-23 artifact installs, verifies and runs.

- Third and fourth audits this run, both clean: AppStream metainfo (11 files, `appstreamcli validate --no-net`) and ELF sonames for the 21 packages that exclude autorequires from their /opt tree. The ELF audit's first pass produced 25 ldd hits; each one was traced and is an alternate-platform or bundle-local artifact, not a missing declaration - ladybird already declares libvulkan.so.1 and openchamber's GTK2 tray libs are never loaded by the app.

- Slice extended while the runner had free slots: after the 23 planned packages, six more (caelestia-cli-mango, cliphist, concat, ghostty, extension-manager, matugen) and six after that (hellwal, localsend, logseq, nwg-look, obsidian, scenefx) were built and installed in fresh containers. All 35 passed rpmbuild -bb, install, rpm -V, ldd and their probe; the extras also put this run's desktop, AppStream and ELF audits on the same artifacts.

- A final wave of six noarch packages (bibata-cursor-theme, cascadia-code-nerd-fonts, freebuff, lazyvim-git, material-symbols-fonts, rustypipe-botguard) took the tear-down total to 41 of 70. Nothing failed: every package rebuilt with `rpmbuild -bb`, installed into a second fresh container, passed `rpm -V` and its probe.
